What causes cancer pain?
Cancer pain can result from the tumor pressing on organs, nerves, or bones.
It may also be caused by cancer treatments like chemotherapy, radiation, or surgery.
Assessing your cancer pain.
there are several tools that can be used to assess pain. for example, Ministry of Health. MOH Pain Scale.
The MOH pain scale combines the NRS VAS, and FACES scale. Patients point to their pain level on a scale from 0 to 10.

For children under 7 and cognitively impaired adults, the IASP faces... pain scale or FLACC scale may be used. In sedated and intubated patients, Pain is assessed through observation, including on behavior.

What should I know about pain-relieving medications?

Medications include over-the-counter pain relievers. For example, paracetamol ibuprofen. Prescription opioids. for example morphine, Oxycodone. Adjuvant medications. for example, antidepressants or anticonvulsants for nerve pain.
If I use morphine, or other opioids for my pain now. Will it be less effective later on when pain gets worse?

No, taking morphine does not mean you are near the end of life. It is used to manage pain and improve comfort any stage of cancer. Many people take it for a long time. while continuing treatment and daily activities.
